title: Retention: own the ritual
source: SILT Plan of Action (Google Doc) + the 24 Nov retention meeting notes
based_on: 2026-11-25 (v3: checked against the detailed meeting notes)
summary: Keep it simple: two cohorts. Cohort 1 is the first week after delivery (unboxing, how to use, setting a routine). Cohort 2 is adherence (helping people keep the routine). Trust and product-education messages go to both. Every message below says who gets it, what it says, when it goes, and how we'll know it worked. Ritual positioning (owning mornings and nights) is the direction the team leaned towards, but the exact benefit language is still open. Everything marked as an idea or open question still needs a decision.
persona: The SILT Nutrition Buddy is a friend, not a parent. Tongue-in-cheek, with corporate puns (stand-ups, EOD reports, blocked calendars), short lines and one idea per message. No fear: it may work short term, but it doesn't build a brand. Images with a few short lines and one interaction tend to get read more than long copy. Every message has English and Hindi (Hinglish) copy. Send Hindi only to customers who asked for it (the first message offers it); never guess from the city. No em dashes, no cure claims, doses exactly as printed on the pack, and every health line checked before it goes live.
decisions: Start with two retention cohorts: First week after delivery, and Adherence.
Trust and product-education messages can go to both cohorts.
For every message, write down who gets it, what they get, when it goes, and the success metric for its cohort.
Draft the messages in English and Hindi, but set each customer's language from their own preference.
Get a Quick Pass demo; it hasn't been looked at properly yet.
Meta stays the near-term acquisition focus.
ideas: Ritual positioning: own the morning and the night, not only functional supplement language.
A first message the day after delivery: "Thank you for being a part of the SILT family".
A short-term cadence of one short message a day or every other day, on a calendar.
A day 4 check-in like "Are your energy levels better?" (wording and metric still to agree).
A ritual newsletter with a memorable name.
A rule of thumb of 2 ROAS after a creative's first week to scale it or replace it. Part of this was unclear in the recording; confirm the exact rule.
Explore ChatGPT ads in 1 to 2 months.
3 to 5 blogs a week from monthly search trends, plus aggregator, marketplace (Amazon, Flipkart) and paid listings for AI search visibility. Target, owner and quality bar not set.
Gamification, a leaderboard and a power-user community (further down this page).
open_questions: Current customer count: both 250 and 280 were said. Also the product mix and the repeat-order rate today.
Which success metric and how many messages a week for each cohort.
WhatsApp message types (utility vs marketing), consent, opt-out handling and send limits.
Which health and product lines are substantiated and approved (each message below lists what to check).
Can Shopify, the Leads tab or Goku reliably give the segmentation fields, and on what consent basis?
Is 2 ROAS after week 1 the agreed rule? Recheck all campaign figures in Ads Manager before using them.
Which game and community ideas are feasible and worth testing first.
What happened with the Quick Pass demo, and what it can really do.

experiment.note: Start with a small, measurable test before any automation.
steps: Send Cohort 1 (r01 to r07) by hand from WhatsApp Business to the next 30 or so deliveries, only to customers who opted in.
Move each of them into Cohort 2 on day 8.
Track replies to r03, r05 and r07, opt-outs, and second orders by the day their box runs out.
Compare second-order rate with customers who got no messages (the ones before the test).
After two weeks, keep what got replies, cut what didn't, then automate.

insights: A team member spoke to about 100 customers. Most hadn't finished their existing supplement stack.
Some weren't regular because of Diwali, travel or routines changing. The product isn't top of mind yet.
Some people may take a supplement break for 3 to 4 months a year (an investor said the same, informally). How common this is for SILT customers isn't known yet; treat it as something to check.
Customer count was given as both about 250 and about 280. At this size the job is the second order; detailed psychographic segmentation can wait until around 1,000 customers.
About 50 customers were said to come from Meta ads. Conversations in the Leads tab may give richer context than ad data alone.

angles.name: Mornings is the hero
angles.detail: Make the first 30 minutes sacred: no phone, one SILT Mornings. Plenty of CEOs guard their first hour; start with 30 minutes.

angles.name: Your calendar is blocked. Mornings and nights are yours.

angles.name: Boring is interesting
angles.detail: Brushing, chai, SILT. The habits that work are the ones you stop thinking about.

angles.name: Mornings benefit language (still open)
angles.detail: Gut health may not feel relevant to someone without a gut complaint. "Feeling refreshed to take on the day" was one suggestion. Any "energy" or before-and-after message has to be clearly defined and supported, using real customer words only.

framework.note: WhatsApp marketing split into cohorts: acquisition, retention and cross-sell. The meeting didn't finalise cadence or metrics, so the frequency and metric in each row are our proposal for the team to confirm. Only the two retention cohorts marked Now are being built.

framework.metrics_note: Metrics discussed: orders per customer, time browsed, sessions created, time on page, checkout progress. A message that brings someone back to the site is an early sign of interest; then look at what they do on the page and whether they check out.

segmentation.note: No psychographic data yet, and at this size we don't need it. Start with basic customer and order data. Together these give the three cuts that make messaging programmatic: who to send to, what to send, and when.

expectations.note: From our website's own timeline. Use it to set expectations, so nobody quits in week one waiting for something that takes a month. The 'you won't feel it' items are what the plan calls the placebo column: they work quietly, so trust content has to carry them.
expectations.rule: For best results, use consistently for at least 3 months (as stated on our site).

messages.goal: Thank you, welcome to the family, and ask their language
messages.image: Unboxing flat lay of the real box with both sticks, warm morning light.
messages.text:
Hi {first_name}, thank you for being a part of the SILT family! 🧡

Your ritual in one line: Mornings any time in the morning, Nights 30 to 60 minutes before bed. One stick, one glass of water, 60 seconds.

We'll check in now and then, like a friend would. Reply STOP any time.

Hindi mein chahiye? Reply HINDI.

SILT Nutrition Buddy
messages.text_hi:
Hi {first_name}, SILT family ka hissa banne ke liye thank you! 🧡

Ritual ek line mein: Mornings subah kabhi bhi, Nights sone se 30 se 60 minute pehle. Ek stick, ek glass paani, bas 60 second.

Hum beech beech mein check-in karenge, ek dost ki tarah. Kabhi bhi STOP reply kar dijiye.

English mein chahiye? Reply ENGLISH.

SILT Nutrition Buddy
branches: HINDI: tag the customer as Hindi; every later message uses the Hindi copy.
No reply: stay on English. Never switch language based on the city alone.
STOP: remove them from every flow straight away.
messages.check: Opt-in and the WhatsApp template category (utility or marketing).

messages.goal: Why 5 g of fibre, and why PHGG
messages.image: The back-of-pack panel, cropped to the fibre line, with an orange marker on "5 g".
messages.text:
Why 5 g of fibre, and why PHGG? 🤓

Most of us eat about 12 g of fibre a day against a 25 to 30 g target. PHGG dissolves thin in water instead of turning to sludge, and it ferments more slowly than inulin in lab tests. So you actually keep drinking it. The right dose, in a form you won't skip.
messages.text_hi:
5 g fibre kyun, aur PHGG kyun? 🤓

Hum mein se zyaadatar log din mein lagbhag 12 g fibre khaate hain, jabki target 25 se 30 g hai. PHGG paani mein ghul jaata hai, gaadha nahi hota, aur lab tests mein inulin se dheere ferment hota hai. Isliye log ise peete rehte hain. Sahi dose, aisi form mein jo aap skip na karein.
messages.check: Health lines to substantiate: the 12 g vs 25 to 30 g fibre figures and their source, and PHGG fermenting more slowly than inulin in lab tests.
messages.metric: Replies; clicks to the lab reports.

messages.image: The Nights pack with four ingredient chips: 3 g glycine, 250 mg magnesium, 300 mg ashwagandha, 200 mg L-theanine.
messages.text: Why is there no melatonin in SILT Nights? 🌙 Because it's a hormone, and we'd rather help your body do its own thing. Instead: 3 g glycine for falling asleep, 250 mg magnesium for recovery, ashwagandha and L-theanine for the racing mind. Every dose is printed on the pack.
messages.text_hi: SILT Nights mein melatonin kyun nahi hai? 🌙 Kyunki woh ek hormone hai, aur hum chahte hain ki aapka body apna kaam khud kare. Iske badle: neend aane ke liye 3 g glycine, recovery ke liye 250 mg magnesium, aur bhaagte dimaag ke liye ashwagandha aur L-theanine. Har dose pack pe likha hai.
messages.check: Ingredient roles (glycine for falling asleep, magnesium for recovery, ashwagandha and L-theanine for a racing mind) against approved wording.

messages.image: A newspaper-style masthead with the newsletter's name and "Edition 1".
messages.text:
60-Second Ritual Read · Edition 1 📰

1. Caffeine has a half-life of about 5 hours, so a 5 PM chai is still half there at 10 PM.
2. Your Mornings stick pairs 80 mg caffeine with 200 mg L-theanine for focus without the jitters.
3. Boring habits win. Same time, same place, every day.

Poll: when's your last caffeine? Reply 1 before noon, 2 by 3 PM, 3 after 3 PM.
messages.text_hi:
60-Second Ritual Read · Edition 1 📰

1. Caffeine ki half-life lagbhag 5 ghante hai, toh shaam 5 baje ki chai raat 10 baje bhi aadhi body mein hoti hai.
2. Aapki Mornings stick mein 80 mg caffeine ke saath 200 mg L-theanine hai: focus, bina ghabrahat ke.
3. Boring aadatein jeet-ti hain. Same time, same jagah, roz.

Poll: aapki aakhri caffeine kab hoti hai? Reply 1 dopahar se pehle, 2 teen baje tak, 3 teen baje ke baad.
messages.check: Caffeine half-life (about 5 hours) and the L-theanine line against approved wording.
messages.metric: Poll replies; site sessions from the link.

messages.trigger: No check-in for 3 days, or a call says they've been irregular
messages.goal: Missed days: no guilt, just restart
messages.text: Missed a few days? Totally normal. Festivals, travel, life. 🙂 No lecture from us. Just pick it up tomorrow morning, and we'll start a fresh streak from day 1.
messages.text_hi: Kuch din miss ho gaye? Bilkul normal hai. Tyohaar, travel, zindagi. 🙂 Hum lecture nahi denge. Bas kal subah se phir shuru kijiye, hum nayi streak day 1 se ginenge.

messages.trigger: Says they're taking a break, or 20 days after running out with no reorder
messages.text: Taking a supplement break? Some people do for a few months a year, and that's your call. Two small things: tell us in one line what made you pause (taste, price, results, or just life). Our founder reads every reply. And when you're back, COMBO10 gets you an extra 10% off the Combo. No spam in between, promise.
messages.text_hi: Supplement se break le rahe hain? Kuch log saal mein kuch mahine ka break lete hain, aur yeh aapka faisla hai. Bas do baatein: ek line mein bataiye kyun ruke (taste, price, results, ya bas zindagi). Hamare founder har reply padhte hain. Aur jab wapas aayein, COMBO10 se Combo pe extra 10% off. Beech mein koi spam nahi, promise.
messages.check: How common supplement breaks are among our customers is unverified, so the wording stays soft.
messages.metric: Replies with a reason; win-back orders.

mechanics.name: Daily check-in: "Kya aapne SILT liya?"
mechanics.how: One nudge at the customer's chosen time. They reply ✅ to log it. Skip days they've already logged, and never send more than two a day.
mechanics.needs: A WhatsApp Business API tool connected to Shopify orders.

mechanics.name: Photo streaks
mechanics.how: To log a day, send a timestamped photo of the morning routine or a sleep-score screenshot at night. Photos and videos earn the same points, to keep it simple. Submissions could become UGC, but only with clear written permission and names hidden. Real screenshots only; we never make or edit them.
mechanics.needs: The WhatsApp tool's media inbox, a simple log, and a permission and privacy note.

mechanics.name: Coins and offers
mechanics.how: Streak days and game scores earn coins; coins unlock offers (the CRED playbook as the analogy).
mechanics.needs: A points sheet to start, then a Shopify loyalty app.

mechanics.name: A nostalgic game
mechanics.how: Ideas: brick breaker (a SILT Mornings paddle breaking "Fatigue in the afternoon" bricks, a few levels), Tetris, Snake, Snakes and Ladders, pinball. On a Shopify tab or behind login, not a separate website.
mechanics.needs: A technical scope (an action item from the meeting).

mechanics.name: Leaderboard and perks
mechanics.how: Scorecards and a leaderboard after login. First name and city only, opt-in.
mechanics.needs: Login on the site, consent, a monthly review.

mechanics.name: Power-user community
mechanics.how: Roughly 50 to 60 power users, possibly split by city.
mechanics.needs: A community admin, moderation rules, incentives.

mechanics_note: All exploratory. Technical feasibility, moderation, incentives, privacy and platform limits haven't been worked out yet.

data.note: Unverified estimates said during the meeting. Don't quote them until they're checked against the source data.
points: Roughly 10,000 people and 14,000 visits, several hundred add-to-carts, and a possible 30% identification rate were mentioned.
The abandoned-cart sheet seems to hold only people who reached checkout and gave a phone number or logged in.
Quick Engage was described as CRM; Quick Pass as login and visitor identification. The claim that Quick Pass captures every visitor's number isn't verified. Hence the demo.
Trade-off: asking for a number early adds friction. A first-purchase incentive or a login flow could help.
Any use of visitor data needs consent and privacy checks first.
ask: For which time windows (30 or 90 days)
How many visitors can actually be identified
What share of visitors or customers gave a login or contact number

setup: Share keyword and search trends weekly (owner to confirm).
Work out the technical approach for gamification (owner to confirm).
Finalise the retention brand language and tone. This tab's English and Hindi copy is the first draft.
Approve the cohort messages here (who, what, when), then load them into the WhatsApp tool as templates. Anything outside the 24-hour reply window needs a pre-approved template.
Ask the data contact the questions in the website data section.
Fix the date and time for the follow-up call once this structure is reviewed (the notes don't record it).
inspiration: Noom for check-ins and honest expectations, CRED for coins and offers, and chai for the ritual itself.
